# RAMalyser

RAMalyser identifies a memory module, checks its wiring, measures its access time in nanoseconds and runs pattern, march, supply-margin and retention tests. It reports each failure by address and data bit.

A [Base unit](reference/glossary.md#term-base-unit) holds the processor, the [Timing engine](reference/glossary.md#term-timing-engine) and the power supplies. Each memory family has a [Cartridge](reference/glossary.md#term-cartridge) that slides into the base unit from the rear.

> [!WARNING]
> **Revision A has never been built**
>
> The boards pass electrical and design-rule checks and the logic passes in simulation. No hardware exists and nothing has been measured. Work through [Bring up a new unit](guides/bring-up.md) before you fit a memory module.
